subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should workspace scanning terminally exclude a subtree for a syntactically valid ignore file that is under 4 MiB but exceeds new rule-count or rule-length limits?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes valid ignore-policy semantics beyond preventing an unbounded file read, and neither current documentation nor established behavior in the supplied evidence defines that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Preserve valid under-cap policies
options.body: Keep the 4 MiB bounded-read protection but remove the new count and per-pattern terminal-denial behavior unless a separately reviewed resource contract requires it.

options.title: Adopt terminal complexity denial
options.body: Approve the broader fail-closed policy, then require explicit upgrade documentation, diagnostics, and exact-head proof for both accepted and rejected ignore policies.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid under-cap policies
recommendation.body: Keep the 4 MiB bounded-read protection but remove the new count and per-pattern terminal-denial behavior unless a separately reviewed resource contract requires it.
